surfaces.note: SURFACE FULLY RECOVERED, AND THE FIX GENERALISES TO ALL OF ai.meta.com. The 400 is not a block on the archive or on the content: ai.meta.com rejects requests that carry a Referer and/or omit Chrome client-hint headers. Sending the complete Chrome header set (sec-ch-ua / sec-ch-ua-mobile / sec-ch-ua-platform / sec-fetch-dest / sec-fetch-mode / sec-fetch-site / sec-fetch-user, accept including image/avif, accept-encoding gzip+br, upgrade-insecure-requests, and NO Referer) returns HTTP 200. fetch.py fails on Meta for two independent reasons, both fixable: (a) its HEADERS dict hard-codes 'Referer': 'https://www.google.com/', and (b) 400 is not in RETRY_STATUS so the ladder never even escalates to Wayback. RESULT: ai.meta.com/blog/ was read LIVE on 2026-08-29 — i.e. the full window tail 2026-08-26..29 that the original sweep could not reach, and in fact the entire window. The index is reverse-chronological (page 1 newest = 'Reimagining Independence… University of Pittsburgh', Jul 27 2026; page 2 runs Oct 2025 – Feb 2026). The newest date appearing anywhere in the page-1 HTML is July 27, 2026. Corroborated independently by Wayback CDX for ai.meta.com/blog/* over 2026-07-15..2026-08-29: the crawler was actively capturing the blog throughout August 2026 and returned only pre-existing slugs — no new post slug appears. CONCLUSION: Meta's AI blog published NOTHING between 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-29. This is now a verified zero from a live read, not an unread surface.

CRITICAL for the open question the blocked-surfaces note left: the five model identities are NOT recoverable, because the AUTHORS ANONYMISE THEM BY DESIGN, not because any surface was unreadable. Verbatim from the Methods: 'We tested five frontier LLMs from two major providers1: Models A and B from Provider 1, and Models C, D, and E from Provider 2.' And footnote 1 verbatim: 'The purpose of this paper is to make a methodological contribution to preference-behavior links in LLMs, so we opt to not reveal specific model provider details.' Consequently the note's contingency 'If the roster is later recovered and names frontier developers, both rows should be re-tiered' can be closed as unreachable. Tier B is correct and FINAL on two independent grounds: §4 condition (b) states outright that 'anonymised' fails, and the paper self-describes as 'a methodological contribution', which puts the models in the role of the INSTRUMENT of a methodology study — an explicit condition (c) exclusion. models_systems should stay empty per §10. Anyone re-screening this should use the arXiv PDF, not OpenReview.

SUGGESTED fetch.py FIXES, both of which cost nothing and would have prevented this whole gap: (1) drop the hard-coded 'Referer': 'https://www.google.com/' from HEADERS, or make it per-call — it is the main reason ai.meta.com 400s; (2) add 400 to RETRY_STATUS so the ladder escalates to Wayback on 400 as it already does on 403 — as written, a 400 surface gets no fallback at all, which is exactly how the Meta blog came to be recorded as unreadable; (3) consider adding the Chrome client-hint headers globally.
